title: Deploy Operation Backend on Railway

input.requestedOutcome: Add the supplied Operation Backend project to a worktree, configure Railway deployment, and merge it into main.
acceptanceCriteria: The application source and Railway configuration are committed.
Railway builds TypeScript, starts the service, and probes /api/health.
Type checking, tests, and the production build pass.
constraints: Preserve the Fastify PORT and 0.0.0.0 runtime behavior.
Do not commit node_modules, build output, or secrets.
assumptions: The repository root is the Railway service source.

output.summary: Committed the supplied Fastify application and added an explicit Railway Railpack build, start, and healthcheck configuration.

filesChanged.purpose: Exclude dependencies, build output, and secrets.
Define build, start, test, and type-check commands.
Define Railway build, start, healthcheck, and restart behavior.
Record task input, output, and evidence.

behaviorChanges.before: No deploy configuration or committed service source existed.
behaviorChanges.after: Railway uses Railpack to run npm ci and npm run build, then npm start with /api/health readiness checks.

details: No schema, migration, or persistence behavior changed.

verification.evidence: Installed 88 packages; npm reported one high-severity audit finding and a blocked optional esbuild install script.

decisions: Use Railpack with explicit npm ci && npm run build.
Use the existing /api/health endpoint for Railway health checks.
risks: The in-process store is not durable across restarts or multiple instances.
npm audit reported one high-severity dependency vulnerability.
dependencies: A Railway project must be created and connected to this repository in the Railway dashboard.
followUps: Replace the in-process store before scaling beyond one instance.
Review and remediate npm audit findings.
rollback: Revert the merge commit or remove the Railway service; no data migration is involved.
